lines.japanese: 「…思ってたより断然いいな」
lines.english: “…This is a lot better than I expected.”

lines.japanese: 「あたしをなめてもらっちゃ困るなぁ」
lines.english: “You really shouldn’t underestimate me.”

lines.japanese: 前回の勉強会から一週間。
lines.english: A week had passed since our last study session.

lines.japanese:
その間で和泉がまとめてきた、
本人曰く『実家から発掘してきた昔の資料群』は、
こちらの予想を遙かに超えた完成度だった。
lines.english: Over that week, Izumi had put together what she called “a cache of old material I dug up at my parents’ house.” It was far more polished than I had ever imagined.

lines.japanese:
とてもレポート提出を一月以上もブッチした、
幽霊ゼミ生が書いた物とは思えないほどに。
lines.english: You would never have guessed it was the work of someone who had been MIA from seminar and blown off her paper for more than a month.

lines.japanese:
「この鬼伝説の別解釈なんかも面白いよな。
最後の方なんか鬼の方に感情移入してるし」
lines.english: “This alternate take on the ogre legend is fascinating. By the end, you’re practically sympathizing with the ogre.”

lines.japanese:
元は、山に棲みついた、人を襲う鬼を討伐する
侍の話なのに、途中から雲行きが怪しくなってくる。
lines.english: It began as the story of a samurai sent to slay an ogre that lived in the mountains and preyed on people. Somewhere along the way, though, things took a strange turn.

lines.japanese:
実は侍は、鬼の女に救われたとか、
その女と愛し合うようになるとか、
逆に女の方が裏切り者として実の姉に処刑されるとか…
lines.english: The samurai was saved by an ogre woman, and the two fell in love, only for her own older sister to execute her as a traitor…

lines.japanese:
「民間伝承にしては勧善懲悪でもないし、
それに随分とロマンチックだし。
…本当に地元でこんな説が根付いてるのか？」
lines.english: “It isn’t exactly a simple tale of good triumphing over evil. It’s remarkably romantic for folklore, too. Do people in the area really tell this version?”

lines.japanese:
「一番有名な異説はさ、鬼が宇宙を放浪する狩猟民族で、
今でも山のどこかに宇宙船と精神体が残ってるって奴で」
lines.english: “The best-known alternate version says the ogres were a race of hunters who roamed the universe, and that their spaceship and disembodied spirits are still hidden somewhere in the mountains.”

lines.japanese:
…異説と言ってる時点で、
一番有名じゃないだろとも思ったけど、
まぁ、そんなのはまったく些末な問題で。
lines.english: Calling it an alternate version suggested it was not, in fact, the best known. But that was entirely beside the point.

lines.japanese:
「…ちゃんと調べてある。
…ように見えなくもない。
かもしれない。けど、いや、まだ予断は…」
lines.english: “…It looks like you did your research. I mean, I guess it doesn’t not look like it. Maybe. Still, I shouldn’t jump to conclusions…”

lines.japanese:
「春希さぁ、どうしてもあたしが怠惰で享楽的な
キリギリスでなくちゃ納得できないわけ？」
lines.english: “Haruki, will nothing satisfy you unless I’m the lazy, pleasure-loving grasshopper from the fable?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、えと…すまん」
lines.english: “No, uh… Sorry.”

lines.japanese:
そんなことより、これを目の前の極楽トンボが
三年前に書いたという事実が、時の流れは残酷だとか、
そういう類の言い回しを彷彿させるのが…
lines.english: More troubling was the fact that the carefree idiot sitting across from me had written this three years ago. It brought certain sayings about the cruelty of time to mind…

lines.japanese:
いや、すまん和泉。
心の中でもう一度謝罪するから許してくれ。
lines.english: No—sorry, Izumi. I apologized again in my head and asked her to forgive me.

lines.japanese:
「ま、昔のあたしは勤勉だったということで。
そのおかげで何の間違いか、峰城に受かっちゃったけど」
lines.english: “Let’s just say I used to be a hard worker. Thanks to that, I somehow even got into Houjou University.”

lines.japanese:
「都内って言ってたっけ。
どこの学校だったんだ？」
lines.english: “You said your school was in Tokyo, right? Which one?”

lines.japanese:
「…都立だよ。何の変哲もないとこ。
学年一桁でないとここには入れないくらいのレベル」
lines.english: “…Just an ordinary public high school. To get into Houjou from there, you had to be one of the top nine students in your grade.”

lines.japanese: …てことは、昔は本当にクラスの優等生で通ってたんだな。
lines.english: So she really had been an honor student back then.

lines.japanese:
「前にも聞いたけどさ、なんで大学入る前に、
こんなマニアックな研究してたんだ？」
lines.english: “I’ve asked you this before, but why were you doing research this niche before you’d even started college?”

lines.japanese:
「ま、そこはね…興味のあるものには
とことんのめり込むタイプだったと言うか…オタク？」
lines.english: “Well, I used to lose myself completely in anything that interested me. You might say I was… a nerd?”

lines.japanese: 「そういう感性こそ大学で発揮しろよ…」
lines.english: “Try showing that kind of dedication in college…”

lines.japanese: 「あ～疲れた。春希、コーヒー」
lines.english: “I’m beat. Coffee, Haruki.”

lines.japanese: 「淹れてやるからそんなにくつろぐな…」
lines.english: “Fine, I’ll make you some. Just don’t make yourself quite so at home…”

lines.japanese:
立ち上がり、大きく背伸びをすると、
和泉はそのまま上半身を仰向けにベッドに投げ出した。
lines.english: Izumi stood, gave an enormous stretch, then flopped backward across the bed.

lines.japanese:
せっかくちょっと見直したのに…
高評価が長続きしない奴だ。
lines.english: Just when I had started thinking better of her… She never let a good impression last.

lines.japanese:
「足しびれた～。駄目だ正座は。
春希～、テーブルと椅子買おうよ。
明日見に行かない？」
lines.english: “My legs are dead. Sitting on my knees is the worst. Haruki, let’s buy a table and chairs. Want to go look tomorrow?”

lines.japanese:
「仕送りのない一人暮らしのバイト苦学生に
無茶な要求をするな。
そもそも和泉のは正座じゃなくて横座りだ」
lines.english: “Don’t ask the impossible of a broke student living alone with no help from home. Besides, you weren’t sitting on your knees. You had your legs tucked off to one side.”

lines.japanese:
「駅前のこんないい場所に住んでるくせに、
ケチケチしなさんなっての」
lines.english: “You live in this great place right by the station. Stop being so stingy.”

lines.japanese:
「駅前のこんないい場所に住んでるから家賃が大変なの。
余計な家財道具を入れる余裕なんかあるか」
lines.english: “And that great location is why the rent is killing me. I don’t have the money or the space for furniture I don’t need.”

lines.japanese:
「そこをなんとか。あたしの顔に免じてさぁ。
春希にはもてなしの心ってやつがわかんないかなぁ」
lines.english: “Come on, do it for me. Have you never heard of being a good host?”

lines.japanese:
「あと、そうやって俺の部屋に
自分の存在を確立させようとするな。
お前が来ていいのはあくまでレポートが終わるまでだ」
lines.english: “And quit trying to establish squatter’s rights in my room. You’re only welcome until that report is finished.”

lines.japanese:
「なんという友達甲斐のなさ。
春希は間違いなくドＳだよね～」
lines.english: “Some friend you are. You’re definitely a sadist, Haruki.”

lines.japanese:
足がしびれたとか言ってるくせに、
この女はベッドの上でそのおみ足をバタバタ暴れさせる。
lines.english: For someone whose legs had supposedly gone numb, she was doing a fine job of flailing those precious limbs all over my bed.

lines.japanese:
「だから人の部屋で暴れるなっての。
みっともない」
lines.english: “I said, don’t thrash around in somebody else’s room. You’re making a spectacle of yourself.”

lines.japanese: 特に今日の…その格好で。
lines.english: Especially dressed like that today.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、和泉」
lines.english: “Listen, Izumi…”
“Slurp… Mmm?”

lines.japanese:
俺の淹れたインスタントコーヒーを受け取ると、
和泉はそのまますぐに口に運んだ。
lines.english: Izumi took the instant coffee I’d made and immediately lifted it to her lips.

lines.japanese:
…今の俺の周りには、
ブラックを好む女が多い。
lines.english: There were an awful lot of women around me these days who took their coffee black.

lines.japanese:
「先週、ウチに来た日のことだけどさ…
ほら、正門で付属のコが待ってて」
lines.english: “About the day you came over last week… You remember the girl from Houjou High waiting at the front gate?”

lines.japanese:
「ああ、一度だけのつもりでついフラフラと
若い肉体に溺れちゃったら、その後もしつこく
関係を迫られて困ってるって言ってたあのコ？」
lines.english: “Oh, the young thing you slept with in a moment of weakness, only to have her keep hounding you for more after you meant it as a one-time thing?”

lines.japanese:
「…多分お前と俺の指している相手は同じなんだろうが、
認識が壊滅的にずれているのをどうにかしてくれ」
lines.english: “…We’re probably talking about the same person, but could you do something about how catastrophically wrong your version is?”

lines.japanese: 「で、そのコがどうしたって？」
lines.english: “So what about her?”

lines.japanese:
「お前…俺とつきあってるって言ったんだって？
彼女に」
lines.english: “You told her… you and I were dating?”

lines.japanese:
「…二度と会うつもりないんじゃなかったっけ？
彼女に」
lines.english: “…I thought you weren’t ever going to see her again?”

lines.japanese:
ちょっとだけ言葉に詰まったけど、
それでも和泉には、何の動揺もなかった。
lines.english: She hesitated for just a moment, but otherwise showed no sign of being rattled.

lines.japanese:
ま、こいつが心乱れたところなんか、
半年以上の付き合いでも未だに見たことないけど。
lines.english: Not that I had seen anything rattle her once in the more than six months I had known her.

lines.japanese:
「偶然会ったんだよ、別の場所で。
そしたら、なんか妙な誤解してて」
lines.english: “We ran into each other somewhere else. She’d gotten completely the wrong idea.”

lines.japanese:
「で、もしかして解いちゃった？
その誤解」
lines.english: “And you didn’t go and correct her, did you?”

lines.japanese:
「解かなくちゃならないだろ普通。
結果的に嘘ついてるってわかったらさ」
lines.english: “What else was I supposed to do? Once I found out I’d been lying to her, I had to set her straight.”

lines.japanese: 「一番あとくされのない手を使ってあげたんだけどなぁ」
lines.english: “I was trying to give you the cleanest possible break.”

lines.japanese: 「あとくされ…」
lines.english: “A clean break…”

lines.japanese:
それどころか、嘘をついたことに、
まるっきり良心の呵責を感じていない。
lines.english: She didn’t feel the slightest twinge of guilt about lying, either.

lines.japanese:
ま、こいつに良心を感じたことなんか、
半年以上の…以下略。
lines.english: Then again, in more than six months I had never seen much evidence that she had a conscience, either… et cetera.

lines.japanese:
「あ～あ、せっかくの処置が台無しだ。
まったく春希ってばお真面目さんなんだから～」
lines.english: “What a waste. There goes a perfectly good solution. Honestly, Haruki, you’re too painfully earnest for your own good.”

lines.japanese:
それどころか、
俺の方こそ空気読めてない痛い奴だったみたいに
呆れた視線を向けてくるに至っては…
lines.english: Worse, she was staring at me in weary disbelief, as if I were the hopeless loser who couldn’t read the room.

lines.japanese: 「なんでそんな…デタラメを？」
lines.english: “Why would you make up something like that?”

lines.japanese: どうしても、責めるような調子にならざるを得ない。
lines.english: There was no keeping the accusation out of my voice.

lines.japanese:
多分、こいつは純粋に
俺のためにやってくれたんだろうってわかっていても…
lines.english: Not even when I knew she had probably done it entirely for my sake.

lines.japanese:
「だぁって春希さぁ、
『女』に触れたくないんでしょ？」
lines.english: “Becaaause, Haruki—you don’t want to so much as touch a ‘woman,’ do you?”

lines.japanese:
「本気になるのが駄目なんでしょ？
女嫌い通り越して、拒否反応出るんでしょ？」
lines.english: “You can’t stand the thought of falling for someone, can you? This goes way beyond hating women. You have an allergic reaction to them.”

lines.japanese:
『純粋に俺のため』とか、
そんな生易しいレベルじゃなかった。
lines.english: This went far beyond doing me a simple favor.

lines.japanese:
「だからこそ、普通の人には女に見えるけど、
春希にだけは女に見えないあたしを
こうして側に置いてる」
lines.english: “That’s exactly why you keep me around. Everyone else sees me as a woman, but you don’t.”

lines.japanese: こ、こいつ…
lines.english: Sh-she…

lines.japanese:
「ならあんたの期待に応えないとね。
春希が『女』に直接触れなくてもいいように、
あたしが防波堤になってあげるよ？」
lines.english: “Then I’d better be what you want me to be. I’ll be your buffer. That way, you never have to touch a ‘woman’ yourself.”
“Izu…mi?”

lines.japanese: いつの間にか、俺を理解してる。
lines.english: Somehow, without my noticing, she had come to understand me.

lines.japanese:
「別に、あんたに女扱いされてないこと、
怒ってもないし、ショックでもないよ。
あたしもそういう関係が嫌いな訳じゃないし」
lines.english: “I’m not angry or hurt that you don’t treat me like a woman. I don’t exactly hate what we have, either.”

lines.japanese:
俺が和泉に感じていた失礼な心地良さを、
完全に見抜いてる。
lines.english: She had seen straight through the insulting comfort I took in being with her.

lines.japanese:
「むしろ春希との今の関係は、
かなり好きな部類に入るし」
lines.english: “Actually, I really like what we have now.”

lines.japanese:
それでいて、女としてのプライドとか、
そういう女っぽい感情をあっさり封じてくれている。
lines.english: And yet she had casually shut away her pride as a woman—all those womanly feelings—for my sake.

lines.japanese:
「だから春希は遠慮なくあたしに逃げればいいよ。
その代わり、レポートと晩ごはんと寝床よろしく」
lines.english: “So run to me whenever you like, Haruki. In return, I expect help with my paper, dinner, and a bed.”

lines.japanese:
それはきっと、本人の言動ほど実は利害の絡まない、
純粋な『俺の不純な動機』への同調。
lines.english: I was sure there was less self-interest in it than her words and actions suggested: pure sympathy with my own “impure motives.”

lines.japanese: そんなに見せてるつもり、なかったのに…
lines.english: I didn’t think I’d let that much show…

lines.japanese:
こいつ、
どうして俺のこと、わかったんだろう。
どこまで俺のこと、わかってるんだろう。
lines.english: How had she figured me out? And just how much did she know?

lines.japanese: 「なぁ、和泉…」
lines.english: “Hey, Izumi…”

lines.japanese: 「なに？　春希」
lines.english: “What is it, Haruki?”

lines.japanese:
「お前さ…
そこまでわかってるんなら、何で…」
lines.english: “If you understand all that, then why…”
“Mmm?”

lines.japanese:
「…今日に限って女の格好してんだよ！
さっきから見えてんだよ！」
lines.english: “…Then why are you dressed like a woman today, of all days? I’ve been able to see your underwear this whole time!”

lines.japanese:
「え～、なに～？
女じゃない奴の生足とかぱんつとか見て嬉しいわけ？
あはははは、あっはははは～」
lines.english: “What, so you enjoy looking at the bare legs and panties of someone who isn’t a woman? Ahahahaha!”

lines.japanese: それなのに…
lines.english: And yet…

lines.japanese:
そこまで俺のこと理解しておきながら、
それでも俺で遊ぶのはなんでなんだよ。
lines.english: If she understood me that well, why did she still insist on toying with me?

lines.japanese:
「彼氏でもない男の部屋で太股を晒すな！
そのまま足を崩すな！　みっともない！」
lines.english: “Don’t sit there flashing your thighs in some guy’s room when he isn’t even your boyfriend! And don’t sprawl out like that! Have some decency!”

lines.japanese:
今日、こいつが俺の部屋に入ってきて最初にしたのは、
エアコンのスイッチを入れ、
設定温度を５度も上げたことだった。
lines.english: The first thing she’d done on entering my apartment that day was turn on the heat and raise the thermostat a full five degrees.

lines.japanese:
で、いぶかしむ俺をよそに、
コートとセーターを脱ぐと、
すぐに自分の部屋のようにくつろぎ始めた。
lines.english: Ignoring my puzzled stare, she had stripped off her coat and sweater and promptly settled in as if the place belonged to her.

lines.japanese:
…キャミソールとミニスカートという、
男の前にしてはあまりにもラフな格好で。
lines.english: A camisole and miniskirt—an absurdly unguarded outfit to wear around a man.

lines.japanese:
「いやもう、
さっきから春希の目のそらし方が可愛くってさぁ。
ついつい必要以上に足開いちゃうんだよね～」
lines.english: “The way you keep looking away is just too cute. Makes me want to spread my legs even wider.”

lines.japanese:
などと言いつつ身体を揺らして笑うたび、
キャミソールに包まれた二つの物体まで揺れやがる。
lines.english: Every time she rocked with laughter, the two things under her camisole bounced right along with her, damn it.

lines.japanese: 「せめてセーターだけは着てくれ。見てられない」
lines.english: “At least put your sweater back on. I can’t keep looking at you.”

lines.japanese:
まさかノーブラじゃないだろうな？
…怖くてとても確かめられないけど。
lines.english: She wasn’t braless… was she? Not that I dared find out.

lines.japanese:
「そうは言ってもさぁ、これただの部屋着だし。
相手が友達だからこそ、こういう格好になるんだって」
lines.english: “But these are just my lounging-around clothes. I’m dressed like this because I’m with a friend.”

lines.japanese:
「それは詭弁だろ。
『親しき仲にも礼儀あり』というワードで検索しろ」
lines.english: “That’s sophistry. Google ‘even close friends need manners.’”

lines.japanese:
「そんなに気になるぅ？
女じゃないのにぃ？
もしかして春希ってバイ？」
lines.english: “Does it bother you that much? Even though I’m not a woman? Haruki, are you bi?”

lines.japanese: 「もうどこから突っ込めばいいのやら…」
lines.english: “I don’t even know where to begin…”

lines.japanese: 『（写真左）峰城大学付属学園入学式にて』
lines.english: ‘Photo, left: the entrance ceremony at Houjou University High School.’

lines.japanese:
『２０○○年４月。
母、曜子の母校でもある峰城大学付属学園に入学』
lines.english: ‘April 20XX. Enrolled at Houjou University High School, also the alma mater of her mother, Youko.’

lines.japanese:
『その実力は、入学時から抜きん出ており、
一年生にして全国コンクール出場を果たす』
lines.english: ‘Her talent stood out from the moment she enrolled, and she competed at the national level in her very first year.’

lines.japanese:
『本選でも審査員の圧倒的支持を受け、優勝。
“学園始まって以来の天才”は、
全国にその名を知られることになる』
lines.english: ‘She won overwhelming support from the judges in the final and took first prize. The “greatest prodigy in school history” became famous throughout Japan.’
“…Yikes.”

lines.japanese: …痒い。
lines.english: …It made me itch.

lines.japanese:
きっとあいつだって、
これを読んだら頭を掻きむしるか、
破り捨てるかの二択だろうな。
lines.english: If she ever read this, she’d either tear her hair out or tear the article to pieces.

lines.japanese:
でも、俺が付属で手に入れた談話をまとめると、
どうしてもこんな提灯記事ができあがる。
lines.english: But once I put together everything people at Houjou High had told me, a puff piece like this was all I could produce.

lines.japanese: 「もうちょっと表現を抑えるか」
lines.english: “Maybe I should tone it down.”

lines.japanese:
取材前から手を加える必要性を感じてたけど、
こっち方向にだとは想定してなかった。
lines.english: Even before the interviews, I’d known the piece would need work. I just hadn’t expected it to need work in this direction.

lines.japanese:
何しろ学園関係者の誰にコメントを求めても、
こういう美辞麗句しか出てこなかった時には、
本気で俺の記憶の方を疑いかけた。
lines.english: Every person I interviewed at the school had offered nothing but glowing praise. By the end, I had started to doubt my own memory.

lines.japanese:
誰もがみな、あいつにした仕打ちも与えた屈辱も、
心の中から綺麗さっぱり洗い流してるみたいだった。
lines.english: It was as though they had scrubbed away every cruelty they’d inflicted on her and every humiliation they’d made her suffer.

lines.japanese:
こういうのがイジメっ子の理論なのかも…
いや、あいつだって全然やられっ放しじゃなかったけど。
lines.english: Maybe that was how bullies remembered things… Though she certainly hadn’t taken it all lying down.

lines.japanese:
「にしても…
つまんなくなりそうだな」
lines.english: “Still… this is going to be boring.”

lines.japanese:
誰もが、ありもしない天才で優等生でお嬢様だった
冬馬を絶賛してた。
lines.english: Everyone was praising a Touma who had never existed: a genius, an honor student, a proper young lady.

lines.japanese:
等身大の冬馬じゃなく、
まるで変身して巨大化したヒーローを見ているかのように。
lines.english: They weren’t remembering Touma as she was, but some superhero who had transformed and grown gigantic.

lines.japanese: でも…
lines.english: But…

lines.japanese: 「…ま、こんなところか」
lines.english: “…Well, that should do it.”

lines.japanese:
事実をねじ曲げていようが、
取材した内容は曲げてない。
lines.english: I might have twisted the facts, but I had not twisted a word of what my sources told me.

lines.japanese:
こんなふうに、
皆の記憶の中に美しく残っているかずさが、
本物の冬馬かずさなら…
lines.english: If the beautiful Kazusa who lived on in everyone’s memories had been the real Kazusa Touma…

lines.japanese:
俺ももう少し、
綺麗に思い出として昇華できたんだろうか？
lines.english: might I have turned my own memories of her into something beautiful too?

lines.japanese:
そんな健全で、あの頃みたいな前向きな自分…
あったらいいとは思うけど、想像はできないな。
lines.english: I wished I could be that healthy, forward-looking person again—the person I had been back then. But I could not even imagine it.

lines.japanese:
「なぁ、和泉。
そろそろ終電じゃないか？」
lines.english: “Hey, Izumi. Isn’t it almost time for your last train?”

lines.japanese:
隣で大人しく推敲をしていた和泉に、
久々に声を掛ける。
lines.english: I spoke to Izumi, who had been quietly revising beside me, for the first time in a while.

lines.japanese:
いつもなら、５分もしないうちに飽きが来て、
雑談と説教で賑やかになる俺たちなのに、
今日は３０分くらい無言の時間が続いてた。
lines.english: Normally she grew bored in under five minutes, and soon the room was full of her chatter and my scolding. Today we had been silent for nearly half an hour.

lines.japanese:
こんなに集中してる和泉は初めてだ。
やっとこの怠け者にも、俺の熱意が伝わったのかと…
lines.english: I’d never seen Izumi concentrate so hard. Maybe my enthusiasm had finally rubbed off on this hopeless slacker…

lines.japanese:
いや、こいつのレポートに俺が熱意持ってても、
しょうがないんだけど。
lines.english: Though there was little point in my being more invested in her paper than she was.

lines.japanese: 「なぁ、和泉って………げ」
lines.english: “Hey, Izumi, are you—oh, come on.”

lines.japanese: 「す～、すぅぅぅぅ～」
lines.english: “Zzz… zzzzz…”

lines.japanese:
さっきから『こんなに集中』していたのは、
どうやら俺の方だったらしい。
lines.english: Apparently I was the one who had been concentrating all this time.

lines.japanese: 「和泉、おい、和泉って」
lines.english: “Izumi. Hey, Izumi.”

lines.japanese:
「ん～、んふ～。
く～、ふぅぅぅぅぅ～」
lines.english: “Mmm… mmh… zzzzz…”

lines.japanese:
もう、レポートの中身はほとんど完成してたので、
俺の出る幕はないと放っておいたのがまずかったか…
lines.english: Her paper was almost finished, so I had figured she no longer needed me and let her be. Apparently that had been a mistake.

lines.japanese:
「そろそろ帰らないと電車なくなるぞ。
早く起きろって」
lines.english: “You’ll miss your train if you don’t leave soon. Come on, wake up.”

lines.japanese: 「ん、んぅ…」
lines.english: “Nn… mmm…”

lines.japanese:
何度肩を揺らしても起きようとしない和泉に痺れを切らし、
机の上の書類を片づけて帰り支度をしようとした時。
lines.english: I shook her shoulder again and again, but she showed no sign of waking. Finally I lost patience and began clearing the papers from the table so I could send her home. That was when…

lines.japanese: 先週より、やけにカバンが大きいことに今さら気づいた。
lines.english: I finally noticed that her bag was much larger than it had been the week before.

lines.japanese:
大学に通学する程度ではまるっきり必要なさそうな、
一泊分くらいの着替えは余裕で入るトラベルバッグ…
lines.english: A travel bag far too large for an ordinary commute to campus—more than big enough to carry a change of clothes for the night…

lines.japanese:
『だから春希は遠慮なくあたしに逃げればいいよ。
その代わり、レポートと晩ごはんと寝床よろしく』
lines.english: ‘So run to me whenever you like, Haruki. In return, I expect help with my paper, dinner, and a bed.’
“…A bed?”

lines.japanese: こいつ…まさか？
lines.english: She hadn’t… had she?

lines.japanese: １．ベッドに寝かせる
lines.english: 1. Put her to bed

lines.japanese: ２．叩き起こす
lines.english: 2. Shake her awake

lines.japanese: 「すぅぅ…ん、んぅ…」
lines.english: “Hnnn… nn… mmm…”

lines.japanese: 「やられた」
lines.english: “She got me.”

lines.japanese: 完全に織り込み済みだ、こいつ。
lines.english: She had planned this from the start.

lines.japanese:
俺の作った夕食（今週もカレー）を余裕でおかわりしたり、
菓子を持ち込んでたり、ビール飲もうとして
俺に説教食らったりとか、全てこのための伏線…？
lines.english: The second helping of my dinner—curry again this week—the snacks she brought, even the beer she tried to drink before I lectured her… Had all of it been setup for this?

lines.japanese:
…ないな。
全部いつも通りだし。
lines.english: …No. That was all perfectly normal for her.

lines.japanese: 「くそっ」
lines.english: “Damn it.”

lines.japanese:
なんて、数時間前の和泉の行動を考察したり、
今の状況に悪態をついたりしても無駄だと悟るしかない。
lines.english: I could replay everything Izumi had done that evening or curse the position she had left me in. Neither would do me any good.

lines.japanese: 今はただ…
lines.english: For now, all I could do was…

lines.japanese: 「触るぞ、許せ」
lines.english: “I’m going to touch you. Forgive me.”

lines.japanese: 「ん…っ」

エアコンを切り、少しでも節電をするためには、
こいつを暖かくリラックスできる場所に運ばないと。
lines.english: If I wanted to switch off the heat and save what little electricity I could, I had to move her somewhere warm and comfortable.

lines.japanese:
まぁ、この部屋でそんな場所なんて、
俺のベッド以外にはあり得ないんだけど…
lines.english: And in this apartment, that could only mean my bed…

lines.japanese:
両脇に手を入れて、テーブルから引きずり出し、
お次は膝に手を入れて抱き上げると…
lines.english: I slipped my hands under her arms and dragged her out from behind the table. Then I put one arm beneath her knees and lifted…

lines.japanese:
今まで知識としてだけで、
体験として知らなかったこいつの身体を感じてしまう。
lines.english: For the first time, I felt the body I’d known until then only in theory.

lines.japanese:
いかん、柔らかい。
完全に俺の想像を超えてる。
lines.english: This was bad. She was soft—far softer than I’d ever imagined.

lines.japanese:
それは、単に肉体が柔らかいというだけじゃなく、
なんというか、身体全体がしなやかで。
lines.english: Not just soft, either. There was a suppleness to her entire body.

lines.japanese:
人形的に言えば可動範囲が広いというか、
人間的に言えば体操選手みたいだというか、
ただの女性の柔らかさ以上のものがあるぞ、こいつ…
lines.english: If she were a doll, I would have said her joints had an unusually wide range of motion. In human terms, she was as limber as a gymnast. There was more to this than the ordinary softness of a woman’s body…

lines.japanese: 「ふぅ…っ」
lines.english: “Whew…”

lines.japanese:
なんて、ちょっと想像の外の葛藤を加えながら、
数秒間の、他の男にとっての天国にして、
俺にとっての苦行は終わった。
lines.english: With that unexpected conflict thrown in, my few seconds of penance—heaven for any other man—came to an end.

lines.japanese: 「ん～、すぅぅ…」
lines.english: “Mmm… zzz…”

lines.japanese:
そんな緊急事態があったことなんか知る由もなく、
相変わらず呑気な寝息を立て続ける和泉。
lines.english: Oblivious to the emergency she had just caused, Izumi went on breathing with the same serene ease.

lines.japanese: 男の部屋に来て、着替えて、飯食って、寝て…
lines.english: She came to a man’s apartment, changed clothes, ate, and fell asleep…

lines.japanese:
って、俺が自分を女扱いしてないことを
知った上での行動だって言うんなら、
辻褄が合わないこともないような気がしないでもないけど。
lines.english: If she was doing all this because she knew I did not see her as a woman, then I could not exactly say it made no sense.

lines.japanese: 「もうちょっとなんとかしようぜ…和泉」
lines.english: “Have a little more sense than this, Izumi…”

lines.japanese:
もし俺が急にその気になったら、
一体どうするつもりなんだよ。
lines.english: What would she do if I suddenly wanted her?

lines.japanese:
…いや、こいつの場合、
『あ～あ、知～らないぞ～』とか言いながら、
普通に許してくれてしまいそうなのが、逆に怖い。
lines.english: No—with Izumi, the truly frightening part was that she might just say, ‘Well, don’t blame me,’ and let it happen.

lines.japanese:
「起きろ！
おい起きろ和泉！」
lines.english: “Wake up! Come on, wake up, Izumi!”

lines.japanese:
肩を揺すったくらいでは起きない和泉に痺れを切らし、
両肩を掴んで上下に強く振る。
lines.english: When shaking her shoulder failed, I lost patience, seized both shoulders, and shook her hard.

lines.japanese: 「あ…すまん」
lines.english: “Oh… sorry.”

lines.japanese:
と、当然の結果として、
テーブルに頭を打つことになるわけで…
lines.english: With the entirely predictable result that I made her bang her head against the table.

lines.japanese:
「いたたたたたたたぁ…
も～、なんなんよ～」
lines.english: “Owwww… Come on, what the hell?”

lines.japanese:
おかげで目が覚めた和泉は、
あくびとも痛みともつかない涙を目尻に浮かべて、
恨みがましい顔で俺を睨みつける。
lines.english: Now thoroughly awake, Izumi glared at me resentfully, tears gathering at the corners of her eyes—whether from pain or a lingering yawn, I couldn’t tell.

lines.japanese: が、今はそんな些末なことを気に掛けている場合ではなく。
lines.english: But this was no time to worry about that.

lines.japanese:
「ヤバいぞおい。
お前、そろそろ終電の時間…」
lines.english: “Oh, shit. Izumi, it’s almost time for your last train…”

lines.japanese: 「…って、何時ぃ？」
lines.english: “…What time is it?”
“…One.”

lines.japanese: 「…終電なら出てから３０分は経過してますが～？」
lines.english: “…The last train left half an hour ago, you know?”
“…Right.”

lines.japanese: これは迂闊だった…
lines.english: That was careless of me.

lines.japanese:
どうやら俺は結構、
自分の仕事に悪戦苦闘していたらしい。
lines.english: Apparently my own work had been giving me more trouble than I realized.

lines.japanese: 「…本当にいいの？」
lines.english: “…Are you really sure?”

lines.japanese:
「ああ、風呂で寝るから。
毛布だけ持ってくぞ」
lines.english: “Yeah. I’ll sleep in the tub. I’m just taking a blanket.”

lines.japanese:
「そりゃまぁ、悪いのは春希だけど、
別に大して怒ってないって」
lines.english: “I mean, sure, this is your fault, but I’m not all that angry.”

lines.japanese:
「…このまま会話を続けると、
俺が大して怒ることになりそうだからやめとこうぜ」
lines.english: “Keep talking and I’m going to get pretty angry, so let’s stop.”

lines.japanese:
この部屋の住民投票では、
『終電の時間を忘れて和泉を起こさなかった俺が悪い』に
いつの間にか一票入っていたみたいだった。
lines.english: The apartment held a two-person referendum. Somehow, one vote had already been cast for “Haruki is at fault for forgetting the last train and failing to wake Izumi.”

lines.japanese:
ちなみにもう一票は、
反論するのがあまりにも馬鹿馬鹿しくて棄権となった。
lines.english: The other voter found the motion too ridiculous to debate and abstained.

lines.japanese:
「お風呂場なんて狭いでしょ？
別にこっちで寝てもいいんだよ？」
lines.english: “The bathroom’s tiny, isn’t it? You can sleep over here too.”

lines.japanese: 「こっちってどっちだよ…」
lines.english: “What exactly does ‘over here’ mean…?”

lines.japanese:
床とそれ以外の場所では、
意味に数億倍の差があるぞ。
lines.english: There were several hundred million shades of meaning between the floor and anywhere else.

lines.japanese: 「どっちでも？」
lines.english: “Either one?”

lines.japanese: 「おやすみ！」
lines.english: “Good night!”

lines.japanese:
…と言いつつ布団を半分開いて
ベッドをぽんぽん叩くのは、
またいつものネタだよなそうだよな？
lines.english: And as she said it, she folded back half the covers and patted the bed. This was her usual routine, right? Just another joke, right?

lines.japanese:
「あっははは…意地になんないでよ春希。
ちょっとした残酷な友情じゃんか～」
lines.english: “Ahahaha… Don’t be so stubborn, Haruki. It’s just friendship with a mean streak.”

lines.japanese: 残酷と言ってる時点でもう…
lines.english: The fact that she called it mean already proved my point…

lines.japanese:
やっぱこいつ、理解のあるふりして
俺をからかってるだろ。
lines.english: She was only pretending to understand me so she could have more fun tormenting me.

lines.japanese:
俺が和泉に女を感じたら、
指差して笑うつもりなんだろ。
lines.english: The moment I saw her as a woman, she meant to point and laugh.

lines.japanese: 「…負けるかよっ！」
lines.english: “…Like hell I’m losing this!”

lines.japanese:
目の前の、男一人が足を伸ばすこともできないスペースが、
何故だかぼやけて見えた。
lines.english: For some reason, the cramped space in front of me—not even long enough for one man to stretch out—began to blur.
“Mmm…”
“Mmm…?”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅ」
lines.english: “Whew.”

lines.japanese:
「あ…っ、
ご、ごめんね、夜遅く」
lines.english: “Oh… I-I’m sorry I’m calling so late.”

lines.japanese:
「ん～。
えっと、誰ぇ？」
lines.english: “Mmm… Um, who is this?”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
「ふあぁぁぁ～。
ごめん、ちょっと寝ぼけてる」
lines.english: “Yaaawn… Sorry, I’m still half asleep.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、あ、あの…
この電話、その、えっと、だから…」
lines.english: “I-I… um… This phone, it’s… I mean…”

lines.japanese:
「あ～、間違い電話？
…今度から気をつけてね～」
lines.english: “Oh, wrong number? Be more careful next time, okay?”

lines.japanese:
「う、ううん、違う…
ここだけは間違えるわけない…」
lines.english: “N-no, that’s not it. This is the one number I couldn’t possibly get wrong…”

lines.japanese:
「じゃあ、誰だっけ～？
も～、勿体ぶらないでよ～」
lines.english: “Then who are you? Come on, don’t keep me in suspense.”

lines.japanese:
「………ううん、いいんです。
ごめんなさい、こんなに夜遅く」
lines.english: “…No. It’s all right. I’m sorry for calling so late.”

lines.japanese: 「何時ぃ？」
lines.english: “What time is it?”

lines.japanese:
「３時…
先週と、同じ…」
lines.english: “Three… The same time as last week…”
“Huh? What is?”

lines.japanese:
「っ…な、なんでもないです。
起こしてしまって本当にごめんなさい。
それじゃ、失礼します」
lines.english: “N-nothing. I’m very sorry I woke you. I’ll let you go.”

lines.japanese: 「あ～い、おやすみ～」
lines.english: “’Kay. Night.”

lines.japanese: 「………おやすみなさい」
lines.english: “…Good night.”

lines.japanese: 「…寝よ」
lines.english: “…Back to sleep.”
“Mmm…?”

lines.japanese: 「お～い春希、起きろ～」
lines.english: “Heeey, Haruki. Wake up.”
“Whuh…?”

lines.japanese:
「開けろ～。
シャワー浴びさせろ～」
lines.english: “Open up. Let me take a shower.”

lines.japanese: 「え、あ、あれ…っ！？」
lines.english: “What? Oh… Wait—?!”

lines.japanese:
見慣れない天井。
聞き慣れない音。
そして、取り慣れない姿勢。
lines.english: An unfamiliar ceiling. An unfamiliar sound. And a position I was most definitely not used to waking up in.

lines.japanese:
切羽詰まっているようで、
どこかのんびりと急かす声に、
俺はゆっくりと体を起こし…
lines.english: The voice urging me to hurry somehow sounded leisurely. I slowly sat up…
“Nnngh!?”

lines.japanese:
そして、つるつるの浴槽に手を滑らせ、
二瞬後、後頭部に鈍痛が走る。
lines.english: My hand slipped on the smooth bathtub. A moment later, a dull pain shot through the back of my head.

lines.japanese:
「うわすごい音したよ…
起きた？　春希？」
lines.english: “Wow, that was loud… Are you awake, Haruki?”

lines.japanese:
「そこは『起きた？』じゃなくて『大丈夫？』だろ。
一宿一飯の恩義的には」
lines.english: “After I fed you and put you up, shouldn’t that be ‘Are you all right?’ rather than ‘Are you awake?’”

lines.japanese: そうだ…
lines.english: Right…

lines.japanese:
とうとう、ただの友達たる和泉に、一飯のみならず、
もう一つの方も差し出してしまったんだっけ。
lines.english: So I had finally given Izumi, supposedly just a friend, both room and board.

lines.japanese:
「わざわざ鍵まで閉めるかなぁ。
そんなにあたしの理性が信用できないわけ？」
lines.english: “Did you really have to lock the door? Do you trust my self-control that little?”

lines.japanese:
主に信用できない（かもしれない）のは
自分側の理性だけど、なら内側から鍵かけても
まったく意味がない矛盾。
lines.english: The problem was, the self-control I couldn’t trust—possibly—was my own. In which case locking the door from the inside accomplished precisely nothing.

lines.japanese: 「…おはよう」
lines.english: “…Morning.”

lines.japanese:
「っていうかよくそんな格好で寝れるね～。
体中痛くない？」
lines.english: “Seriously, how did you sleep like that? Doesn’t your whole body hurt?”

lines.japanese:
こんな格好で寝れたのは、
冬の朝ですら少し明るくなってきた頃。
lines.english: It had been nearly dawn—even a winter morning was beginning to brighten—before I managed to fall asleep like that.

lines.japanese:
それに、今は後頭部の痛みのおかげで
他の痛みが全て吹き飛んでいる。
lines.english: Besides, the pain in the back of my head had eclipsed every other ache.

lines.japanese: 「今、何時？」
lines.english: “What time is it?”

lines.japanese:
「ん、８時。
急げば春希の大好きな朝イチの講義も間に合うよ？」
lines.english: “Eight. Hurry and you can still make that first lecture you love so much.”

lines.japanese: 朝イチだけじゃなく、講義はどれも大好きだ。
lines.english: I loved all my lectures, not only the first one.

lines.japanese: 「ふあぁぁぁぁぁ～」
lines.english: “Yaaaaawn…”

lines.japanese:
聞かれたことに頭の中でしか答えられないくらい、
相当に寝ぼけているらしいな、俺。
lines.english: Apparently I was so groggy I could answer her only inside my own head.

lines.japanese:
「シャワー借りるよ。
あとトーストは２枚。目玉焼きは両面。
ソース派だから塩コショウ勝手にかけないでね」
lines.english: “I’m taking a shower. Two slices of toast, and fry my egg on both sides. I want mine with sauce, so don’t put salt and pepper on it.”

lines.japanese: 「…朝食用意すること前提なのな」
lines.english: “And naturally, I’m the one making breakfast.”

lines.japanese: 卵あったっけなぁ…
lines.english: Did I even have any eggs?

lines.japanese:
「モタモタしないで出ていく。
まぁ、一緒に入るって言うなら止めないけどさ～」
lines.english: “Quit dawdling and get out. Unless you want to join me—I won’t stop you.”

lines.japanese: 「俺が止め…脱ぎ出すな！」
lines.english: “I’m the one who’s stopping you—don’t start undressing!”

lines.japanese:
キャミソール一枚だと、
一瞬でヤバい領域に突入するって言うのに
こいつときたら…
lines.english: With nothing but a camisole on, she’d enter dangerous territory in under a second. And yet…

lines.japanese:
「あっははは。
ホント春希のリアクションは面白いねぇ」
lines.english: “Ahahaha! Your reactions really are priceless, Haruki.”

lines.japanese: ほんの一瞬だけど見えちまったじゃないか。
lines.english: Because, if only for a second, I had caught a glimpse—

lines.japanese:
「…もう二度と泊めないからな。
来週からは終電逃したら外で寝ろ。
お前の大好きな寝袋を用意しといてやる」
lines.english: “…I’m never letting you stay again. From next week on, miss your train and you sleep outside. I’ll have your beloved sleeping bag ready.”

lines.japanese:
…用意した着替えの中に、
しっかりいつもの長袖シャツとパンツという、
ちゃんとセクシーさを抑えた服が入っていたのを。
lines.english: —of her usual long-sleeved shirt and pants tucked among the clothes she had packed: an outfit chosen to keep her sex appeal safely under control.

lines.japanese:
「あ～、そういえばさ、
もしかしたら、春希に謝らなくちゃならないかも」
lines.english: “Oh, that reminds me. I might owe you an apology.”

lines.japanese: 「確定してることをいかにも可能性っぽく語るな」
lines.english: “Don’t dress up a certainty as a maybe.”

lines.japanese:
もはや、突っ込みどころが多すぎて、
どこから指摘してどこを怒ればいいのやら…
lines.english: There were so many things to object to now, I hardly knew where to begin or what to be angriest about.

lines.japanese:
「春希、携帯部屋に置いてったでしょ？
夜中に一度かかってきてさ、あたし出ちゃったんだよね」
lines.english: “You left your phone in the room, remember? It rang once in the middle of the night, and I answered it.”

lines.japanese:
「そんな些細なことを謝るつもりがあるなら、
もう少し俺にかけてる迷惑の量と質をだなぁ…」
lines.english: “If you’re going to apologize for something that minor, maybe start with the quantity and sheer quality of all the other trouble you cause me…”

lines.japanese:
「女の子からでさ、
あたしの声聞いたら、なんかえらく慌てちゃって」
lines.english: “It was a girl. The moment she heard my voice, she got awfully flustered.”
“…What?”

lines.japanese:
「今朝着信見たら…おぎそ…ゆきな？
そんな感じの名前のコ」
lines.english: “I checked your call log this morning… Ogiso… Yukina? A name like that.”

lines.japanese: 「ゆきな…」
lines.english: “Yukina…”

lines.japanese: それは、雪に菜っ葉と書いて『せつな』。
lines.english: Written with the characters for snow and greens, but pronounced Setsuna.

lines.japanese: 「夜中の３時だったから、もしかしたら緊急かも」
lines.english: “It was three in the morning, so it might have been an emergency.”
“Three…”

lines.japanese: 今朝の３時ってことは、水曜２７時。
lines.english: Three that morning—in other words, Wednesday, 27:00.

lines.japanese: それってつまり、先週のその時間は…
lines.english: Which meant that, at the same time last week…

lines.japanese:
「後でフォロー入れといた方がいいかも。
もしかしたら妙な誤解されてるかもしんないし」
lines.english: “You might want to smooth things over later. She could have gotten the wrong idea.”

lines.japanese:
「いや………必要ない。
大丈夫だ」
lines.english: “No… There’s no need. It’s fine.”

lines.japanese:
「そう？
なんならあたしが直接フォローしても…」
lines.english: “Are you sure? I could explain it to her myself if you want.”

lines.japanese: 「必要ないって言ってるだろ」
lines.english: “I said there’s no need.”
“…Fine.”

lines.japanese: その可能性に思い至らない訳じゃなかった。
lines.english: It wasn’t as though the thought had never occurred to me.

lines.japanese:
先週の、あのやりとりは、
俺たちにとって、久しぶりに共有した、
楽しくてかけがえのない時間だったから。
lines.english: That exchange the week before had given us a happy, irreplaceable moment together—the first in a long time.

lines.japanese:
少なくとも、俺にはそう感じられたし、
雪菜だって、そう感じてくれた…と思う。
lines.english: At least, that was how it had felt to me. And I thought—hoped—that Setsuna had felt it too.

lines.japanese:
たった一度の連絡が、
俺たちをほんの少し疎遠でなくさせた。
lines.english: That one exchange had made us a little less distant.

lines.japanese:
だから、もしもう一度連絡があったら。
俺はきっと、前より抵抗なく通話ボタンを押せていた。
lines.english: So if a call had come through to me, I was sure I could have pressed the answer button with less hesitation than before.

lines.japanese:
そして、そのまま二度、三度と何気なく続いていけば、
もしかしたら、三年前の俺たちに遡る道が
開けたのかもしれなかった。
lines.english: And if we had gone on like that, casually keeping in touch a second time, then a third, perhaps a road back to who we had been three years ago might have opened.

lines.japanese: けれど、結果はそうじゃなかった。
lines.english: But that wasn’t what happened.

lines.japanese:
一つ目の点は穿たれた。
けれど、二つ目の点は“偶然”消えてしまった。
lines.english: The first point had been marked. But “chance” erased the second.

lines.japanese:
だから点は線にならず、
やっぱり俺たちは、繋がらないままだった。
lines.english: So the points never became a line, and we remained unconnected.

lines.japanese:
「じゃあ今日はここまで。
名簿前まで持ってきてください」
lines.english: “That’s all for today. Please bring the attendance sheet to the front.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅ」
lines.english: “Whew.”

lines.japanese:
本日三コマ目の講義も終わり、
日も結構西側に傾いてきた。
lines.english: My third class of the day was over, and the sun was already well on its way down.

lines.japanese:
今日はこの後に取っている授業はないし、
この後、研究室に顔を出して…
lines.english: I had no more classes, so next I would stop by the seminar room and…

lines.japanese:
「なぁ和泉。
お前のレポートだけど、荻島教授に中間報告…」
lines.english: “Izumi. About your paper—I want you to give Professor Ogishima a progress report…”

lines.japanese: 「…すぅ」
lines.english: “…Zzz.”

lines.japanese:
そういえば…
お隣は、出席名簿にチェック入れてから、
ずっと机に突っ伏していたような。
lines.english: Come to think of it, she had marked herself present and then spent the entire lecture facedown on her desk.

lines.japanese:
それも、昼飯後で陽気のいい
この三コマ目だけならともかく、
午前中の二つの授業のときも始めから終わりまで…
lines.english: And not only this warm, post-lunch third period. She’d done the same thing from beginning to end in both morning classes.

lines.japanese: 「おい」
lines.english: “Hey.”
“Mmm…”

lines.japanese:
硬い浴槽の中で明け方まで苦しみ首筋まで痛めた俺が
こうしてちゃんと起きてるというのに、
人のベッドでのうのうと寝てた奴がこの体たらく…
lines.english: I had suffered in a hard bathtub until dawn and wrenched my neck, yet here I was, awake and attending class. She had slept in my bed without a care in the world, and this was the result…

lines.japanese:
「起きろ！
この三限寝太郎！」
lines.english: “Wake up, you third-period Rip Van Winkle!”

lines.japanese:
などと、昨夜のことを思い出すたびに、
こうして理不尽な怒りに身を任せそうになる。
lines.english: Every time I remembered the night before, I came dangerously close to giving myself over to this completely unreasonable anger.

lines.japanese:
「たたた…
も～、なんなの春希ぃ」
lines.english: “Ow, ow… What was that for, Haruki?”

lines.japanese: …今、ちょっとだけ任せたけど。
lines.english: …Though just now, I had given in for a moment.

lines.japanese:
「とっくに講義終わってるんだよ。
お前は一体どこまで育つつもりだ？」
lines.english: “The lecture ended ages ago. Just how much more growing do you plan to do?”

lines.japanese:
「なに？
やっぱお風呂入ってるとき覗いたの？」
lines.english: “What? So you did peek while I was in the shower?”

lines.japanese:
「俺は身長のことを言ってるだけだ。
性的な意味など一切ない」
lines.english: “I was referring strictly to your height. There was no sexual meaning whatsoever.”

lines.japanese:
「ふあぁ…ええと、何限目が終わったって？
今何時？」
lines.english: “Yaaawn… Which class did you say was over? What time is it?”

lines.japanese: 「三限目。２時４０分過ぎ」
lines.english: “Third period. It’s after two forty.”

lines.japanese:
「もうそんな時間かぁ。
今日は朝からよく勉強した～」
lines.english: “That late already? Boy, did I study hard this morning.”

lines.japanese:
「本当に期待を裏切らないコメントだな。
これからゼミ行くぞ」
lines.english: “You never fail to live down to my expectations. We’re going to the seminar.”

lines.japanese:
「あ～、行ってらっしゃい。
あたしは帰って寝直すわ」
lines.english: “Have fun. I’m going home to finish my nap.”

lines.japanese:
「お前も行くんだよ。当然だろ。
せっかくちゃんとレポートやってんだから、
教授に進捗報告をだな…」
lines.english: “You’re coming too. Obviously. You’ve finally made real progress on your paper, so you need to update the professor…”

lines.japanese:
「そんなの春希がやっといてよ。
あたしが報告するより、あんたから言った方が
教授も信じるでしょ」
lines.english: “You do it. The professor’s more likely to believe you than me.”

lines.japanese:
「その壊滅した信頼関係を
少しでも回復したいとか思わないのかよ？」
lines.english: “Don’t you want to win back even a little of the trust you’ve completely destroyed?”

lines.japanese:
「大学なんて在籍できてりゃいいのよ。
それじゃお休みなさい」
lines.english: “As long as I stay enrolled, that’s good enough for me. Good night.”

lines.japanese:
「こら起きろ和泉！
お前、このままじゃ卒業もおぼつかないって、
本当にわかって…」
lines.english: “Wake up, Izumi! Do you realize you might not even graduate at this rate—”

lines.japanese:
「お、やっと見つけた！
春希～！」
lines.english: “There you are! Haruki!”
“Takeya…?”

lines.japanese:
教室から出て行くばかりの人波に逆行して、
昔から見慣れた姿と聞き慣れた声が近づいてくる。
lines.english: A familiar figure and voice approached against the tide of students pouring out of the classroom.

lines.japanese:
「お前、探したぞ。
なんでこんな北の最果てにこそこそ隠れてんだよ」
lines.english: “I’ve been looking everywhere for you. Why are you hiding all the way up here at the north end of nowhere?”

lines.japanese:
「それはな、ここ３号館が
俺のホームグラウンドだからだ」
lines.english: “Because Building Three happens to be my home turf.”

lines.japanese:
大学の北端にある３号館は文学部の校舎。
こいつらのいる政経の６号館は大学の南端。
lines.english: Building Three, home of the Faculty of Literature, stood at the university’s northern edge. Political Science and Economics occupied Building Six at the southern edge.

lines.japanese:
「いつの間にか文学部なんかに逃げやがって。
おかげで金借りることもままならないだろ」
lines.english: “You went and hid in someplace like Literature without warning. Now I can barely even borrow money from you.”

lines.japanese:
だから、片方に明確な目的がない限り、
もう俺たちは偶然顔を合わせることは、ほとんどない。
lines.english: Unless one of us had a specific reason to seek out the other, we almost never met by chance anymore.

lines.japanese:
「で、いくらだ？
悪いけど万は貸せないぞ。
あと、返済期限は今年中に…」
lines.english: “How much do you need? I can’t lend you ten thousand yen. And I want it back before the end of the year…”

lines.japanese:
「そんなケチな用事で来てねえよ。
メシなら曜日ごとに食わせてくれるコが７人いる」
lines.english: “I didn’t come all this way for something that petty. I’ve got seven girls who feed me, one for every day of the week.”

lines.japanese:
「…お前はどうして
今でも依緒と友達でいられるんだろうな」
lines.english: “…How are you still friends with Io?”

lines.japanese:
最初は反動とか反抗とか反応待ちとかだったのに、
いつの間にかライフワークに近くなってるような。
lines.english: At first it had been rebound, rebellion, or fishing for a reaction. Somewhere along the way, it seemed to have become his life’s work.

lines.japanese: ま、反応してやらない依緒も悪いんだけど。
lines.english: Though Io shared the blame for refusing to give him the satisfaction of a reaction.

lines.japanese:
「と、それより今は俺じゃなくて春希のことだ。
…お前、一体何言ったんだよ？」
lines.english: “Never mind me. Right now this is about you. What the hell did you say to her?”

lines.japanese: 「…何も」
lines.english: “…Nothing.”

lines.japanese:
武也の、主語をわざと外した言い回しとその表情で、
こいつが誰のことを言ってるのかわかってしまうのが、
自分でも嫌になる。
lines.english: I hated myself for knowing exactly who he meant from the name he had deliberately left out and the look on his face.

lines.japanese:
「そんなはずないだろう。
お前らと何年一緒にいると思ってんだよ？」
lines.english: “Don’t give me that. How many years do you think I’ve known the two of you?”

lines.japanese:
「本当に何も言ってない。
それどころかここ一週間話してもいない。
…少なくとも俺は」
lines.english: “I really haven’t said anything. We haven’t spoken all week… At least, not from my end.”

lines.japanese:
今日は、もう木曜日。
あれから１６８時間は経過した。
lines.english: It was Thursday already. A full hundred and sixty-eight hours had passed.

lines.japanese:
「じゃあ、逆パターンか？
またシカトしたのかお前？」
lines.english: “So it was the reverse this time? You ignored her again?”

lines.japanese:
「………そんなことしてない。
自発的には」
lines.english: “…I didn’t ignore her. Not on purpose.”

lines.japanese:
まったく意図しない偶然の結果としてそうなったからって、
俺が武也に責められる謂われはないはずだ。
lines.english: It had happened entirely by accident, with no intention on my part. Surely that meant Takeya had no right to blame me.

lines.japanese:
「なんでだよ春希…
いつまでこんな状態続けるんだよ？」
lines.english: “Why, Haruki? How long are you going to let this go on?”

lines.japanese: 「何もしてないって言ってるじゃないか」
lines.english: “I keep telling you, I haven’t done anything.”

lines.japanese: …フォローもしてないけど。
lines.english: Though I hadn’t followed up with her, either.

lines.japanese:
「あんないいコいないだろ…
出さえすりゃ絶対ミス峰城取れるくらい可愛くて、
なのに家庭的で、一途で…おかしいぞあのバランスは」
lines.english: “There isn’t another girl like her. She’d win Miss Houjou hands down if she ever entered, but she’s great around the house, she’s devoted… That combination just isn’t fair.”

lines.japanese:
「そうだよ。俺とはレベルが違うんだ。
最初から交わるはずがなかったんだよ、俺たち」
lines.english: “Exactly. She’s out of my league. Our paths were never supposed to cross in the first place.”

lines.japanese: 「…本気で言ってるのか？」
lines.english: “…Do you honestly mean that?”

lines.japanese: 「武也、俺は…」
lines.english: “Takeya, I…”

lines.japanese:
「…って、お前が自分の言ったことを
冗談だなんて認める訳ないわな」
lines.english: “…Right. As if you’d ever admit something you said was a joke.”

lines.japanese:
武也とは…武也や依緒とは、
数え切れないくらい、もう何度もこの話になった。
lines.english: Takeya and I—or rather, Takeya, Io, and I—had been through this more times than I could count.

lines.japanese:
「でも、雪菜ちゃんだって認めるわけがないんだよ。
お前のこと嫌いなんて。二度と会いたくないなんて」
lines.english: “But Setsuna would never say she hates you, either. Or that she never wants to see you again.”

lines.japanese:
俺たち三人の関係も、
俺が雪菜にした仕打ちも、
その後の俺の最低な対応も。
lines.english: They knew about the three of us: what I had done to Setsuna, and the vile way I had treated her afterward.

lines.japanese:
「で、俺は春希と雪菜ちゃんのどっちを選べと聞かれたら、
そりゃもう、迷いなく彼女についてくって決めてる訳」
lines.english: “If anyone asked me to choose between you and Setsuna, I wouldn’t even have to think about it. I’d side with her.”

lines.japanese:
俺の最低な部分を全部知ってるこいつらは、
俺が全面的に悪いってことも知っていながらも、
それでも必死に俺たちの橋渡しをしようとしてくれる。
lines.english: Takeya and Io knew every ugly part of me. They knew the blame was entirely mine. Even so, they kept trying desperately to build a bridge between us.

lines.japanese:
「依緒だって同じこと言ってる。
だからな春希、お前がいくら駄々こねようと、
俺たちの中じゃもう過半数は取れてんだよ」
lines.english: “Io says the same thing. So kick and scream all you like, Haruki—we already have a majority vote.”

lines.japanese:
まだ、俺が彼女に償う道はあるはずだって。
その道は、俺だけじゃなく、彼女も救うはずだって。
lines.english: They believed there must still be some way for me to atone to her. That the same path would save her as well as me.

lines.japanese:
「もう一度、ちゃんと話せって。
今のお前たち、見てられないんだよ」
lines.english: “Talk it out with her, just once more. We can’t stand watching the two of you like this.”

lines.japanese:
そんな、露悪的なくらいに都合のいい夢物語を、
今でも頑なに信じてるらしい。
lines.english: Even now, they clung stubbornly to that shamelessly convenient fairy tale.

lines.japanese: …自分たちのことを棚に上げて。
lines.english: Conveniently ignoring their own situation.

lines.japanese:
「とにかく、近いうちに連絡入れるんだぞ？
なんなら俺がセッティングしてやっても…」
lines.english: “Anyway, call her soon, all right? If you want, I can set the whole thing up myself…”

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、武也…」
lines.english: “Listen, Takeya…”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 『ありがとう』
lines.english: Thank you.

lines.japanese:
「悪い。
そろそろゼミあるから」
lines.english: “Sorry. I’ve got a seminar to get to.”

lines.japanese: 「春希っ！」
lines.english: “Haruki!”

lines.japanese:
本当に、武也のお節介が嬉しかった。
きっと裏で糸を引いている依緒の思いやりも嬉しかった。
lines.english: I truly was grateful for Takeya’s meddling. I was grateful too for Io’s kindness, because she was surely behind it.

lines.japanese:
けれど俺はもう、
そんな尊いものを向けられていい奴じゃないから。
lines.english: But I was no longer the kind of person who deserved anything so precious from either of them.

lines.japanese:
「また今度飲もう。電話する。
…たまには男同士差し向かいでな」
lines.english: “Let’s have a drink another time. I’ll call. Just the two of us, man to man, for once.”

lines.japanese:
だってこいつは…こいつらは、知らないんだ。
俺が本当は、どんなことをしでかしてしまったのかを。
lines.english: Because he… because neither of them knew what I had really done.

lines.japanese:
そう、こいつらは、知らないんだ。
あの時の雪菜を。
lines.english: No. They didn’t know the Setsuna I had seen that day.

lines.japanese:
その傷が、いつか塞がるなんてとても信じられない、
最後の最後の、本当に最後に顔を出す、真実の雪菜を。
lines.english: They did not know the real Setsuna, the one who had emerged only at the very, very end, bearing a wound I could not believe would ever close.

lines.japanese:
「だから待てっての！
まだ話は終わってないんだって」
lines.english: “I told you to wait! I’m not finished yet.”

lines.japanese:
「なら手短に話せよ。
前振り長すぎるんだよ」
lines.english: “Then get to the point. Your setup was way too long.”

lines.japanese:
「彼女さ、今週の土曜、
医学部の男連中とのパーティに出るんだとさ。
主催の奴ら、さっきからもうこの話で持ちきりで」
lines.english: “She’s going to a party with a bunch of guys from the med school this Saturday. The organizers have been talking about nothing else.”

lines.japanese:
「パーティくらい普通だろ？
何慌ててんだよ？　自分が行けないからか？」
lines.english: “There’s nothing unusual about going to a party. Why are you panicking? Because you can’t go?”

lines.japanese:
「確かに男は医学部しか行けないけど…
俺の言いたいのはそんなことじゃなくて」
lines.english: “Sure, the men have to be medical students, but that’s not what I’m trying to tell you.”

lines.japanese:
「合コンみたいなものだろ？
そんな程度でこの剣幕だったのかよ？
いくら雪菜だからって…」
lines.english: “It’s basically a singles mixer, right? You came storming over here for that? Even if it is Setsuna…”

lines.japanese:
「俺が手に入れた情報だと、
そのパーティ、ちとヤバいかもしれないんだよ」
lines.english: “From what I’ve heard, that party might be bad news.”

lines.japanese:
「相手がウチの医学部じゃなぁ。
俺たちが張り合おうにも、肩書きじゃ勝負にならないな」
lines.english: “We’re talking about our own med school. We can’t exactly compete with those credentials.”

lines.japanese:
「確かに…
女の子の方でもチケット手に入れるの結構難関らしい。
まぁ、雪菜ちゃんは主催が口説き落とした方だけど」
lines.english: “True… Apparently the tickets are hard for women to get too. Though in Setsuna’s case, the organizer talked her into coming.”

lines.japanese:
「そりゃ仕方ないだろ。
悔しかったら医者になれ。
俺は血が苦手だから御免だけど」
lines.english: “Nothing to be done about that. If you’re jealous, become a doctor. I can’t stand blood, so count me out.”

lines.japanese:
「だから、ヤバいってそういう意味じゃなくて…
女の子騙して薬使うって、そっち方向。
麻酔とか、ハイになる奴とか」
lines.english: “I don’t mean dangerous like that. I mean they trick girls and drug them—anesthetics, stuff that gets them high.”

lines.japanese:
「………都市伝説だろ。
医学部に対するやっかみから生まれた」
lines.english: “…That’s an urban legend born from resentment of medical students.”

lines.japanese: 「まぁ、今のところ、半々…より、ちょい下くらい？」
lines.english: “Maybe. At this point I’d say the chances it’s true are… a little under fifty-fifty?”

lines.japanese:
「くだらねぇ。
医学部の奴らには黙っといてやるから、
あんま広めるなよ？」
lines.english: “That’s ridiculous. I won’t tell anyone in the med school you said it, so don’t spread it around.”

lines.japanese: 「…心配じゃないのか？」
lines.english: “…You’re not worried?”

lines.japanese: 「ガセネタ相手に何を心配しろって？」
lines.english: “What am I supposed to worry about over a bogus rumor?”

lines.japanese:
「御宿の菱島ビル５階にある
イタリアンレストランで１９時から。
場所は、東口の一番奥の２３番出口から…」
lines.english: “Seven o’clock, at the Italian restaurant on the fifth floor of the Hishijima Building in Onjuku. From Exit 23, all the way at the far end of the east side…”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあな」
lines.english: “See you.”

lines.japanese: 「春希…」
lines.english: “Haruki…”

lines.japanese: 「あ、終わった？」
lines.english: “Oh, are you done?”

lines.japanese: 「聞いてた？」
lines.english: “Were you listening?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ？」
lines.english: “Who knows?”

lines.japanese:
武也が俺に近づいてきたときには、
既に和泉は俺から離れ、
さっさと教室の外に出てしまっていた。
lines.english: By the time Takeya approached me, Izumi had already moved away and slipped out of the classroom.

lines.japanese:
で、話が終わるまで、
どうやら大人しく教室の外で暇を持て余していたらしい。
lines.english: Apparently she had been killing time quietly outside, waiting for us to finish.

lines.japanese: 「ま、別にいいけど」
lines.english: “Well, it doesn’t matter.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、その台詞、なんかあたしっぽい」
lines.english: “Oh, that sounded like something I’d say.”

lines.japanese:
「知るか。
ゼミ行くぞ」
lines.english: “Like I care. We’re going to the seminar.”
“Mm…”

lines.japanese:
研究室へと向かう俺の足音にほんの少し遅れて、
当然のように、もう一つの足音が続く。
lines.english: A second set of footsteps fell in behind mine, only a beat late, as naturally as though there had never been any question.

lines.japanese: さっきまで帰る気満々だったくせに。
lines.english: Even though she’d been determined to go home only minutes ago.

lines.japanese:
「やっぱさ…
電話した方がいいんじゃない？」
lines.english: “Still… don’t you think you should call her?”

lines.japanese: 「…聞いてた？」
lines.english: “…You were listening?”
“…Who knows?”

lines.japanese:
武也や依緒みたいな昔からの友達とも、
同じ学部の友達とも違うこの距離感が、
今の俺には、ほんの少しだけありがたい。
lines.english: The distance between us was unlike what I shared with old friends like Takeya and Io, and unlike the easy familiarity of friends in my own department. Just then, I was a little grateful for it.

lines.japanese:
こうしたさり気ないフォローも、
深く関わってまではいないけど、
空気だけは感じ取ることのできる、こいつにしか…
lines.english: Only she could offer that kind of quiet support: not involved deeply enough to interfere, but close enough to feel the air change…

lines.japanese: 「あ、ところでさ、春希」
lines.english: “Oh, by the way, Haruki.”
“What?”

lines.japanese:
「９９００円貸してくれない？
二年参りの時に返すから」
lines.english: “Could you lend me 9,900 yen? I’ll pay you back when we go to the shrine to ring in the New Year.”

lines.japanese: 「聞いてただろ全部」
lines.english: “You heard every word.”
